questions.question: A new manager at a community recycling center wants volunteers to help double the amount of material collected this year. Which approach would best enlist their support?

options.A: Ask for their ideas and share progress
options.C: Wait until the year ends to discuss it
options.D: Tell them the goal isn't their concern

questions.explanation: Ask for their ideas and share progress. Asking volunteers for ideas makes them part of the plan, which increases their commitment, and sharing progress shows how their efforts matter. Volunteers in particular need to feel ownership, since they aren't paid to stay. Assigning goals without discussion can feel like orders, saying the goal isn't their concern excludes them, and waiting until the year ends to discuss it removes any chance to adjust. Leaders who enlist others well listen, share credit and keep everyone focused on a goal they helped shape.

performanceIndicator.text: Enlist others in working toward a shared vision

questions.question: When looking for a specific figure in a long report, a reader should first

options.A: read every page from the start.

questions.explanation: Check the contents or index. The table of contents and index show where topics appear, so a reader can go straight to the right section instead of reading everything. Reading every page wastes time when only one figure is needed, skipping the report means not finding the information, and guessing risks using a wrong number. Skimming headings, charts and summaries are other useful strategies for extracting relevant information quickly, especially when a decision or meeting is coming up soon.

performanceIndicator.text: Extract relevant information from written materials

questions.question: An employee who volunteers to help with a new project and asks questions to learn more is showing
questions.explanation: Interest and enthusiasm. Volunteering and asking questions show that the employee cares about the work and wants to contribute, which demonstrates interest and enthusiasm. Boredom and frustration would show up as low effort or complaints, dependence means relying on others, and resistance to change means avoiding new things. Enthusiastic employees often energize their teams, and managers frequently give them new opportunities because they seem ready to learn and grow. Some employers ask applicants to show enthusiasm by preparing questions about the company. Enthusiasm is contagious, so it often improves a team's overall energy.

questions.question: When explaining a store policy to an upset customer, an employee should

options.A: blame the manager for the rule.
options.C: read the policy and walk away.

questions.explanation: Explain it and offer options. Customers accept policies more easily when employees explain them calmly and respectfully and offer whatever options are available, such as an exchange or store credit. Reading the policy and walking away feels dismissive, blaming the manager makes the business look divided, and refusing to discuss the policy frustrates the customer further. Explaining the reason behind a policy, such as hygiene rules for returned swimwear, can also help customers understand and accept it. Knowing the policy well beforehand makes these conversations easier.

questions.question: A hiring manager is choosing between two candidates with equal skills. Which personality trait would most likely make one stand out as the better employee:
questions.explanation: Dependability. Dependable employees arrive on time, keep commitments and complete work accurately, so managers and coworkers can rely on them. Impatience can lead to rushed work and conflicts, arrogance makes teamwork difficult, and carelessness causes mistakes that cost time and money. Other desirable traits include honesty, flexibility, friendliness and a positive attitude. Employers often ask interview questions designed to reveal these traits, such as asking for examples of times a candidate kept a difficult commitment.

performanceIndicator.text: Identify desirable personality traits important to business

questions.question: A small business pays its monthly rent by having its bank move money electronically from its account to the landlord's account. This form of financial exchange is a(n)
questions.explanation: Electronic funds transfer. An electronic funds transfer moves money from one bank account to another electronically, without paper checks or cash. Automatic rent payments, direct deposit of paychecks and online bill payments are common examples. A cash payment uses physical money, a credit card purchase borrows money from the card issuer, and a money order is a prepaid paper payment bought from a bank or post office. EFTs are fast and create a clear record, which helps businesses track payments and avoid late fees.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain forms of financial exchange (cash, credit, debit, electronic funds transfer, etc.)

questions.question: During a job interview for a hotel front desk position, Gavin wants to show enthusiasm. Which action would best accomplish this?

options.A: Ask when the interview will be over
options.B: Look at his phone between questions
options.C: Smile and explain why he wants the job
options.D: Answer every question with one word

questions.explanation: Smile and explain why he wants the job. Smiling, making eye contact and explaining specific reasons he wants the job, such as enjoying helping travelers, shows genuine interest and enthusiasm. One-word answers suggest low interest, looking at his phone signals that he isn't paying attention, and asking when the interview will end makes him seem eager to leave. Researching the hotel before the interview gives him specific details to mention, which makes his enthusiasm more convincing to the interviewer. Sending a thank-you note after the interview reinforces his interest.

questions.question: A new employee notices that her manager keeps glancing at the clock and gathering papers while she explains a long idea. Which of the following is the best way for her to respond:

options.A: Speak louder to regain his attention
options.B: Keep talking until she covers every detail
options.C: Summarize quickly and offer to follow up
options.D: Ask him why he seems so rude

questions.explanation: Summarize quickly and offer to follow up. Glancing at the clock and gathering papers usually signal that someone is short on time. Summarizing the main point and offering to follow up later respects the manager's schedule while still sharing the idea. Continuing with every detail ignores the cues, speaking louder doesn't solve the time problem and may seem pushy, and calling him rude turns a simple signal into a conflict. Reading nonverbal cues helps employees adjust their communication in the moment, which makes conversations more productive for both people.

questions.question: When the price of a popular toy rises sharply because supply is limited, the higher price mainly

options.A: causes the toy to disappear from markets.
options.B: tells stores to stop ordering it.
options.C: signals producers to make more of it.
options.D: guarantees that no one will buy it.

questions.explanation: Signals producers to make more of it. In a market economy, prices send signals. A rising price shows that demand is greater than supply, which encourages producers to make more because they can earn higher profits. The higher price also rations the limited supply among buyers willing to pay more. It doesn't guarantee that no one buys the toy, tell stores to stop ordering it or make it disappear. As supply increases over time, the price usually falls back toward normal levels.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the functions of prices in markets

questions.question: When a supervisor gives several oral directions quickly, an employee should

options.B: take notes and repeat the steps back.
options.C: nod and hope to remember everything.
options.D: ask a coworker to listen instead.

questions.explanation: Take notes and repeat the steps back. Writing down key steps and repeating them back confirms that the employee heard and understood the directions correctly, and it gives the supervisor a chance to fix any misunderstanding right away. Nodding and hoping to remember often leads to forgotten steps, starting early can mean missing important details, and asking a coworker to listen shifts the employee's responsibility to someone else. Asking clarifying questions about anything unclear is also part of following oral directions well.

questions.question: A manager tells Ellis to restock aisle 3, then price the new shipment, and finally clean the break room before 5 p.m. Ellis finishes the first task and forgets the others. Which habit would most likely have prevented this?

options.A: Writing down each step as he heard it
options.B: Asking a coworker to finish his tasks
options.C: Working faster on the first task
options.D: Waiting for the manager to remind him

questions.explanation: Writing down each step as he heard it. Writing down multi-step directions as they are given creates a checklist Ellis could follow after the manager leaves. Asking a coworker to finish his tasks shifts his responsibility, working faster on the first task doesn't help him remember the others, and waiting for reminders makes the manager do extra work. Many employees use a small notebook or phone notes for this purpose. Repeating the steps back to the manager before starting is another simple way to make sure nothing is forgotten.

questions.question: The first step in solving a business problem is to

options.A: wait for the problem to go away.

questions.explanation: Identify the problem clearly. Problem solving starts with clearly identifying what is wrong, because a solution aimed at the wrong problem won't help. The next steps typically include gathering information, generating possible solutions, choosing and carrying out the best one, and evaluating the results. Picking the cheapest solution skips analysis, blaming someone doesn't fix anything, and waiting for problems to go away often lets them grow. Many businesses use a standard problem-solving process so teams approach issues consistently.

questions.question: A pharmacy employee notices that many customers wait in line just to pick up prescriptions that are already filled. She suggests adding a pickup locker that customers open with a code. Which of the following does her suggestion best demonstrate:
questions.explanation: Innovation skills that improve service. The employee spotted a problem, long lines for simple pickups, and suggested a new solution that could save customers time. That is innovation in action. Her idea welcomes change rather than resisting it, it shows responsibility rather than avoiding it, and it goes beyond simply following directions. Businesses benefit when employees at every level notice problems and propose practical improvements, which is why many companies reward employee suggestions that are put into practice. Her idea also frees pharmacists to spend more time with patients who need advice.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the need for innovation skills

questions.question: Jordan's pay stub for one pay period shows gross pay of $720, federal income tax of $58, Social Security and Medicare of $55, and a health insurance deduction of $27. What is Jordan's net pay?
questions.explanation: $580. Net pay equals gross pay minus all deductions: $720 - $58 - $55 - $27 = $580. The answer $720 is gross pay before deductions. $607 subtracts only taxes and Social Security and Medicare but forgets the health insurance, and $662 subtracts only federal income tax. Checking each deduction on a pay stub helps employees catch errors, such as a wrong tax amount or a benefit they didn't sign up for, and plan their budgets around the money they actually receive.

questions.question: Dani feels her face getting hot when a customer criticizes her work. She takes a deep breath, listens to the full complaint and responds calmly. Which of the following parts of emotional intelligence is she showing:
questions.explanation: Self-regulation. Self-regulation means managing one's emotions so they don't control one's actions. Dani notices her anger, pauses and chooses a calm response, which helps her handle the complaint professionally. Technical expertise involves job skills, time management involves organizing tasks and deadlines, and physical fitness involves the body's health and strength. Self-regulation is especially valuable in customer-facing jobs, where reacting emotionally can turn a small complaint into a lost customer or a public conflict. Taking a breath before responding gives the thinking part of the brain time to catch up.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the nature of emotional intelligence

questions.question: A warehouse requires employees to wear steel-toed boots and complete forklift training before operating equipment. Which of the following best describes these requirements:
questions.explanation: Safety regulations. Health and safety regulations are rules designed to protect workers from injury and illness. Steel-toed boots protect feet from heavy objects, and forklift training prevents accidents with dangerous equipment. Many of these rules come from OSHA, while others are company policies. Marketing guidelines, customer service policies and pricing strategies deal with customers and sales rather than worker safety. Following safety regulations reduces injuries, lowers insurance and workers' compensation costs and helps businesses avoid fines.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe health and safety regulations in business

questions.question: A word-processing feature that automatically creates personalized letters for hundreds of customers from a list of names and addresses is
questions.explanation: Mail merge. Mail merge combines a standard letter with a data source, such as a spreadsheet of customer names and addresses, to create a personalized copy for each person. It saves hours compared with typing each letter separately. Spell check finds misspelled words, word count totals the words in a document, and page numbering adds numbers to each page. Businesses use mail merge for invitations, thank-you letters and notices that need the same message with different details.

questions.question: A warehouse worker who believes her employer is ignoring serious safety hazards can file a complaint with the
questions.explanation: Occupational Safety and Health Administration. The Occupational Safety and Health Administration, or OSHA, creates and enforces rules to protect workers from hazards, such as unsafe machinery, toxic chemicals and falls. It also inspects workplaces and can fine employers that break safety rules. The Federal Communications Commission regulates communications, the Food and Drug Administration oversees food and medicine safety, and the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission enforces laws against workplace discrimination. Many businesses post OSHA safety information where employees can see it.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe health and safety regulations in business

questions.question: Rosa is emailing a proposal to a client and wants her supervisor to receive a copy without the client seeing the supervisor's address. Which of the following email features should she use:
questions.explanation: Bcc. Bcc, or blind carbon copy, sends a copy to someone without the other recipients seeing that person's address. Cc, or carbon copy, shows every recipient who else received the message. Reply all responds to everyone on an existing email, and forward sends a received message to someone new. Bcc is also useful when emailing large groups, because it protects recipients' addresses from being shared with everyone on the list. Using Bcc for a manager should be done honestly and in line with company policy.

questions.question: Kenji must decide which of two delivery services his flower shop should use. His first step in the decision-making process should be to
questions.explanation: Define the problem or decision. Clearly defining the problem or decision makes sure a person is solving the right issue and helps guide the rest of the process. The next steps usually include gathering information, identifying alternatives, evaluating them, choosing one and reviewing the results. Choosing the first available option skips evaluation, asking a friend to decide avoids responsibility, and acting without planning often leads to poor results. Good decision makers take time at the start to understand exactly what needs to be decided.

questions.question: Mateo works at a car dealership that allows business casual clothing. Which of the following outfits best maintains an appropriate personal appearance for his job:

options.A: A formal tuxedo with a bow tie
options.B: Khaki pants and a collared shirt

questions.explanation: Khaki pants and a collared shirt. Business casual usually means neat pants, such as khakis, and a collared shirt or blouse, without the formality of a suit. That outfit looks professional to customers while fitting the dealership's dress code. A wrinkled, stained shirt looks careless, gym shorts and sandals are too casual and may be unsafe on a lot with vehicles, and a tuxedo is far too formal for daily work. Employees' appearance affects how customers judge a business, which is why many companies explain their dress codes during orientation.

questions.question: In a database, all the information about one customer, such as name, address and phone number, makes up a
questions.explanation: Record. A record is a complete set of related information about one item or person, such as one customer. Each piece of information within the record, such as the last name, is stored in a field. A spreadsheet cell is the intersection of a row and column, and a query result is the set of records a search returns. Understanding records and fields helps employees enter data correctly and search databases effectively, for example to find every customer in one city.

questions.question: A shopper who pays with a debit card is

options.A: paying with a store gift card.
options.B: borrowing money she will repay later.
options.C: using a check written from her savings.
options.D: spending money from her bank account.

questions.explanation: Spending money from her bank account. A debit card takes money directly from the cardholder's checking account, usually within a day or two, so the shopper spends money she already has. Borrowing money to repay later describes a credit card. A check is a written order to a bank to pay someone, and a gift card holds a prepaid amount for a specific store. Because debit card purchases come straight from a bank account, users should track spending carefully to avoid overdraft fees when the balance runs low.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain forms of financial exchange (cash, credit, debit, electronic funds transfer, etc.)

questions.question: Which word-processing feature would help a writer make sure every heading in a long report looks the same:

options.A: Using the space bar to center text

questions.explanation: Applying heading styles. Heading styles apply the same font, size and formatting to every heading with one click, and changing the style updates all headings at once. Styles can also build an automatic table of contents. Bolding headings by hand is slow and easy to do inconsistently, using the space bar to center text produces uneven spacing, and printing the report several times doesn't change its formatting. Consistent formatting makes reports easier to read and look more professional.

questions.question: The ability to recognize and manage one's own emotions and understand the emotions of others is called
questions.explanation: Emotional intelligence. Emotional intelligence includes self-awareness, self-control, motivation, empathy and social skills. People with strong emotional intelligence notice how they feel, manage their reactions under stress and read others' feelings accurately. Technical skill involves job-specific abilities, physical stamina is endurance for physical tasks, and academic knowledge comes from study. Employers value emotional intelligence because it helps people work well in teams, handle conflict calmly and serve customers effectively, even when situations are tense. Unlike some traits, emotional intelligence can be improved with practice and feedback.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the nature of emotional intelligence

questions.question: A professional email to a client should include

options.A: messages written in all capital letters.
options.D: no greeting or signature at all.

questions.explanation: A clear subject line. A clear subject line tells the reader what the email is about before opening it, and a polite closing with the sender's name and contact information looks professional. Slang and emojis are usually too casual for client emails, all capital letters can seem like shouting, and leaving out a greeting and signature makes the message seem abrupt. Professional emails are also concise, proofread before sending and organized so the main point appears early. Reading an email once more before sending catches most typos and missing details.

questions.question: A smart thermostat that a homeowner can adjust from a phone app while away is an example of
questions.explanation: The Internet of Things. The Internet of Things refers to everyday devices, such as thermostats, doorbells and appliances, that connect to the internet to send and receive data. A smart thermostat lets users control temperature remotely and track energy use. A printed newsletter, a landline telephone and a paper calendar don't connect to the internet. Businesses use connected devices too, such as sensors that track inventory or equipment performance, which is one reason the internet's scope keeps growing.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the scope of the Internet

questions.question: On a pay stub, the amount an employee earns before any deductions are taken out is
questions.explanation: Gross pay. Gross pay is the total amount earned before deductions such as taxes, Social Security, Medicare and benefits. Net pay, or take-home pay, is what remains after deductions. Overtime pay is extra pay for hours worked beyond the normal schedule, and year-to-date tax shows how much tax has been withheld so far this year. Reading a pay stub helps employees check that they were paid correctly and understand where their money goes. Errors are easier to fix when they are caught on the first pay stub.

questions.question: Ramon needs to email a client to reschedule a meeting. Which of the following subject lines is most effective:

options.B: Hey, quick thing about our meeting

questions.explanation: Rescheduling Thursday's Meeting. An effective subject line is specific, so the client knows exactly what the email is about and can find it later. "Rescheduling Thursday's Meeting" does both. "Hey, quick thing about our meeting" is too casual and vague, "Important!!!" creates false urgency and gives no information, and "Question" is too vague to be useful. Busy professionals often decide which emails to open first based on subject lines, so clear ones get faster responses and help the sender look organized.

questions.question: For a job interview at a bank where employees wear business attire, the most appropriate choice is

options.C: a costume to stand out from others.

questions.explanation: A pressed business suit. Interviewers form first impressions quickly, and dressing like the employees at the workplace, or slightly more formally, shows respect and seriousness about the job. A clean, pressed suit or business outfit fits a bank's business-attire culture. Jeans with a T-shirt and athletic clothes are too casual, and an attention-grabbing costume would seem unprofessional. Good grooming, such as neat hair and clean shoes, matters as much as the clothing itself. Applicants who aren't sure of a company's dress code can ask the recruiter beforehand.

questions.question: During a team discussion about a new expense policy, one member, Aiden, hasn't spoken. Which of the following would best encourage him to participate:

options.A: Asking him directly for his opinion
options.B: Ignoring him so he doesn't feel pressured
options.D: Telling him he should talk more

questions.explanation: Asking him directly for his opinion. A friendly, direct invitation, such as "Aiden, what do you think about this?" gives a quieter member a clear opening to share ideas. Some people won't interrupt but have valuable input when asked. Ignoring him means the group misses his ideas, telling him he should talk more can embarrass him, and ending the meeting early doesn't solve anything. Good discussion leaders make sure everyone has a chance to contribute, which leads to better decisions.

questions.question: After a drought damages much of the nation's wheat crop, the price of bread rises, and some shoppers switch to rice and potatoes. Which function of prices does this best illustrate?
questions.explanation: Rationing a scarce product. Higher prices help ration scarce products by encouraging some buyers to purchase less or switch to substitutes, which leaves the limited supply for those who value it most. Shoppers switching to rice and potatoes is a clear example. Higher prices don't guarantee bakery profits, since costs also rose, they don't eliminate competition, and prices clearly aren't staying the same. This function of prices helps markets adjust to shortages without government rationing. Price signals guide decisions throughout the economy without any central planner.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the functions of prices in markets

questions.question: When creating presentation slides, a speaker should

options.A: use many different fonts on each slide.
options.B: read every slide word for word.
options.D: use few words and clear visuals.

questions.explanation: Use few words and clear visuals. Effective slides support the speaker rather than replacing him or her. A few key words and clear visuals, such as charts and photos, help the audience follow along and remember the main points. Paragraphs of text overwhelm viewers, reading slides word for word bores the audience, and mixing many fonts makes slides look cluttered. A common guideline is to keep each slide focused on one idea, which also helps the speaker stay organized. Practicing with the slides beforehand helps the speaker keep to the time limit.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the internet:

options.B: A software program for writing documents
options.C: A single computer owned by one company
options.D: A private network for one school only

questions.explanation: A global network of networks. The internet is a worldwide network that connects millions of smaller computer networks, allowing people and businesses to share information, communicate and buy and sell products. No single computer or company owns it. A word-processing program is software that runs on a computer, and a private school network is an intranet, which connects users within one organization. The internet supports email, websites, video calls, online shopping and connected devices around the world. Businesses rely on it for everything from email to cloud storage and online sales.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the scope of the Internet

questions.question: Nadia has 15 minutes before a meeting to find last year's market share figures in a 70-page industry report. Her manager wants to compare the company's share with that of its two largest competitors. Which strategy is most effective?

options.A: Ask the meeting to be postponed
options.B: Print the report to read later
options.D: Read the report from the beginning

questions.explanation: Scan headings and charts. Scanning headings, charts and tables helps Nadia find specific numbers quickly, since market share data is often shown in a chart or summarized in a labeled section. Reading from the beginning would take far longer than 15 minutes, printing the report doesn't help before the meeting, and postponing the meeting is unnecessary. She could also use the document's search function for a term like "market share." Extracting relevant information efficiently is a valuable skill for busy professionals.

performanceIndicator.text: Extract relevant information from written materials

questions.question: A customer wants to return an opened package of earbuds, saying he opened them only to check the color. The store's policy doesn't allow returns of opened earbuds for hygiene reasons, and the customer is upset. What is the best response?

options.A: Say nothing and wait for him to leave
options.B: Accept the return without telling anyone
options.C: Explain why and suggest an exchange
options.D: Tell the customer the policy is unfair

questions.explanation: Explain why and suggest an exchange. Explaining the hygiene reason helps the customer understand the policy, and suggesting an exchange for a defective product, if allowed, offers a helpful solution. Accepting the return secretly breaks the policy and treats customers inconsistently, calling the policy unfair undermines the business, and staying silent ignores the customer. Employees who interpret policies clearly and courteously can often keep upset customers satisfied, even when the answer isn't what they wanted. A manager may also have authority to make exceptions in unusual cases.

questions.question: A store manager wants to find every customer in the database who made a purchase over $500 last year. Which of the following database functions should he use:
questions.explanation: Run a query. A query searches a database for records that meet certain conditions, such as purchases over $500, and displays only those records. Sorting by name only reorders the records, deleting records would destroy data, and printing the entire database would make the manager search by hand. Queries let businesses quickly create targeted lists, for example to invite top customers to a special sale, which makes database skills useful in many jobs. Saved queries can be run again each month to update the list automatically.

questions.question: During tax season, Oakview Tax Services receives twice as many complaints about slow email replies as last year, and two longtime clients have moved to a competitor. The manager identifies the cause: one employee answers all client emails, about 120 a day, while four others mostly answer phones, which ring far less often than they used to. What is the next logical step?

options.A: Ignore the complaints during tax season
options.B: Fire the employee who handles email
options.C: Develop ways to share the workload

questions.explanation: Develop ways to share the workload. Once the problem and its cause are known, the next step is developing possible solutions, such as sharing email duties, using templates for common questions or setting response-time goals. The manager can then choose the best option and track whether complaints drop. Ignoring complaints during the busiest season could lose clients, firing the employee punishes someone for a staffing problem, and stopping email responses would make the problem worse. Systematic problem solving leads to lasting fixes.

questions.question: A caller asks a receptionist about a large order, but the person handling orders is out for the day. Which of the following is the most businesslike response:

options.B: Hang up and let the caller try again
options.C: Take a message and promise a callback
options.D: Tell the caller to try another company

questions.explanation: Take a message and promise a callback. Taking a detailed message, including the caller's name, number and question, and promising a callback from the right person keeps the customer's business and shows professionalism. Sending the caller to another company loses a sale, guessing at order details could give wrong information, and hanging up is rude. The receptionist should also tell the caller when to expect the callback and make sure the message reaches the right person promptly. Reading the message back to the caller confirms that the details are correct.

performanceIndicator.text: Handle telephone calls in a businesslike manner

questions.question: During a meeting, a client leans back, crosses his arms and stops making eye contact while a salesperson explains a price increase. These cues most likely suggest that the client is
questions.explanation: Unhappy or unconvinced. Nonverbal cues such as crossed arms, leaning away and avoiding eye contact often signal discomfort, disagreement or doubt, which makes sense when someone hears about a price increase. Eagerness to sign usually shows through leaning in, nodding and asking about next steps. Nothing suggests confusion about the meeting time, and a pleased client would more likely smile and stay engaged. A salesperson who notices these cues can pause and ask a question, such as "What concerns do you have?", instead of continuing to talk past the client's reaction.

questions.question: Akira is preparing a five-minute presentation on monthly sales for her company's leaders. Which of the following would make her slides most effective:

options.B: One simple chart per main point
options.C: Every number from the sales database

questions.explanation: One simple chart per main point. A short presentation to busy leaders should highlight the most important information clearly. One simple chart per main point, such as sales by region, makes trends easy to see. Twenty slides of detailed tables are too much for five minutes, every number from the database overwhelms the audience, and animated effects on every word distract from the message. Akira can bring detailed reports as handouts for anyone who wants more information after the presentation.

questions.question: Managers often look for employees with an achievement orientation, meaning people who

options.C: wait for others to set every goal.

questions.explanation: Set and pursue challenging goals. Achievement orientation is the drive to meet and exceed high standards. Employees with this trait set challenging goals, track their progress and look for ways to improve. Doing only the minimum, avoiding difficult work and waiting for others to set every goal show low motivation to achieve. Employers value achievement-oriented employees because they often produce strong results and take on more responsibility, though these employees also need realistic goals to avoid burnout. They also tend to look for feedback so they can keep improving.

questions.question: Joaquin manages a bakery and must decide whether to open on Mondays. He has listed his options and gathered sales data from nearby stores. Opening Mondays would require two extra staff members at a cost of about $300 per day. What should he do next in the decision-making process?

options.B: Weigh each option's pros and cons
options.D: Ask customers to make the decision

questions.explanation: Weigh each option's pros and cons. After defining the problem, gathering information and listing alternatives, the next step is evaluating each option's advantages and disadvantages, such as added sales versus extra labor costs. Then Joaquin can choose the best option and later review the results. Choosing randomly wastes the work he has done, ignoring the data defeats the purpose of collecting it, and letting customers decide gives away a management responsibility, though their feedback can be part of the evaluation.

questions.question: Marcus's goal is to sign up 30 new gym members this month. With ten days left, he has already signed 29. Which response best shows an achievement orientation?

options.A: Tell coworkers he's done for the month
options.B: Set a higher personal target for the month
options.C: Lower his goal for next month

questions.explanation: Set a higher personal target for the month. An achievement orientation means continuing to push for excellence even after a goal is nearly met. Setting a higher personal target, such as 40 members, keeps Marcus motivated and shows initiative. Stopping recruiting or telling coworkers he's done wastes ten days of opportunity, and lowering next month's goal sets a weaker standard. Managers notice employees who exceed goals, which can lead to bonuses and new responsibilities. Achievement-oriented employees still need realistic targets so they stay motivated without burning out. She might also share what is working with coworkers so the whole team benefits.

questions.question: An insurance agent is about to email a signed policy to a client. Before clicking send, she should

options.A: check that the correct file is attached.
options.C: send it to every contact in the address book.

questions.explanation: Check that the correct file is attached. Attaching the wrong file, or forgetting the attachment, can confuse the client, delay work and even share confidential information with the wrong person. Checking the attachment before clicking send prevents these mistakes. Deleting the subject line makes the email harder to understand, sending it to every contact spreads it to people who shouldn't receive it, and removing the greeting and signature makes it look unprofessional. Many email programs now warn users when a message mentions an attachment that isn't included.

questions.question: A store manager who wants employees to support her vision of becoming the top-rated store in the region should first

options.A: announce it once and never mention it again.
options.B: explain the vision and why it matters.
options.C: keep the vision secret until it is reached.

questions.explanation: Explain the vision and why it matters. People commit to a shared vision when they understand it and see why it matters, both to the business and to them. Explaining the vision, such as better reviews leading to more customers and job security, gives employees a reason to care. Keeping it secret makes it impossible to work toward, punishing questions discourages involvement, and mentioning it only once lets it fade. Effective leaders repeat the vision often, connect daily tasks to it and celebrate progress so employees stay motivated.

performanceIndicator.text: Enlist others in working toward a shared vision

questions.question: Employers increasingly rank innovation skills among the abilities they want most, mainly because employees with these skills can

options.D: find new ways to solve problems.

questions.explanation: Find new ways to solve problems. Innovation skills include creativity, curiosity and problem solving, which help employees find better products, services and processes. As customer needs and technology change, businesses need people who can adapt and suggest new ideas. Avoiding change, following only written instructions and working without training don't describe innovation. Many employers now list creativity and problem solving among the top skills they want in new hires, because innovative employees help companies stay competitive. Showing initiative like this can also lead to new projects and promotions.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the need for innovation skills

questions.question: A manager describes an employee as someone who adjusts quickly when plans change and is happy to take on different tasks when needed. Which personality trait is the manager describing?
questions.explanation: Flexibility. Flexibility means adapting willingly when plans, tasks or priorities change. Employees with this trait help their teams handle surprises, such as covering for an absent coworker. Stubbornness is resistance to change, shyness is discomfort in social situations, and impulsiveness means acting without thinking things through. Flexibility is especially valuable in businesses with changing schedules or customer demands, and employers often look for it when hiring for fast-paced jobs. Flexible employees are often the first people managers ask when new opportunities come up.

performanceIndicator.text: Identify desirable personality traits important to business

questions.question: When a receptionist at Lakeside Printing picks up a ringing business line, her first words to the caller should

options.A: greet the caller and name the company.
options.B: ask the caller to call back later.
options.C: put the caller on hold without speaking.

questions.explanation: Greet the caller and name the company. A professional greeting, such as "Good morning, Lakeside Printing, this is Maria," tells the caller he or she reached the right business and sets a courteous tone. Asking the caller to call back or putting him on hold without speaking can frustrate the caller, and answering with "Yeah?" sounds unprofessional. After the greeting, the employee should listen carefully, take notes and offer help or transfer the call to someone who can assist. Smiling while speaking makes a voice sound friendlier, even on the phone.

performanceIndicator.text: Handle telephone calls in a businesslike manner

questions.question: During a group discussion about a new schedule, an effective participant

options.B: shares ideas and listens to others.

questions.explanation: Shares ideas and listens to others. Effective group discussion depends on sharing ideas and listening carefully to others, which helps the group consider different views and reach better decisions. Interrupting cuts off others' ideas and creates tension, staying silent means the group loses one person's input, and talking about unrelated topics wastes time. Good participants also ask questions, build on others' ideas and help the group stay on track toward its goal. Taking brief notes during the discussion also helps participants respond thoughtfully. Groups that hear every member's view usually make better decisions.
